title: Shuffle Into a Palindrome
statement:
You get a string s of lowercase letters. You may reorder its letters any way you like, but you must use every letter exactly as many times as it appears.

Return true if some ordering reads the same forwards and backwards, and false otherwise.

examples.why: "abcba" works. One letter with an odd count can sit in the middle.
Both c and d appear once. Only one letter can go in the middle.
a appears 3 times and b once: two odd counts. Checking only "at most one letter appears once" would wrongly accept it.

constraints: s has only lowercase English letters
hints: In a palindrome, each letter on the left half has a partner on the right half. What does that say about counts?
Every letter must appear an even number of times, except possibly one letter that sits in the very middle.
Count letters, or simply toggle each letter in a set: whatever is left in the set has an odd count. Answer whether at most one is left.

explain.intuition:
A palindrome pairs position i with its mirror position. Every letter is used in pairs, except the single middle letter of an odd-length string. So the order of s does not matter at all; only how many letters have an odd count. Zero or one odd count: possible. Two or more: impossible.

A neat way to track parity is a set used as a toggle: add a letter the first time, remove it the second time, add it again the third time. At the end the set holds exactly the letters with odd counts.
steps: For each letter: if it is in the set, remove it; otherwise add it.
pitfalls: Counting letters that appear exactly once, instead of letters with an odd count. "aaab" has one single letter but two odd counts.
Requiring zero odd counts. Odd-length palindromes have one letter in the middle.
Actually generating permutations, which is factorial time.

solutions.title: Count and check parity
solutions.idea: Count each letter, then count how many counts are odd.

solutions.title: Toggle set
solutions.idea: Add a letter when you see it, remove it when you see it again. Only odd-count letters remain.

followups: Use a single 26-bit integer instead of a set. What operation toggles one bit?
Return every distinct palindrome you can build from the letters.
